questions.q: What does a ServiceNow certification actually, reliably demonstrate?
options: A guaranteed job offer at a specific employer
Verified baseline knowledge against a published, standardized exam blueprint, which can help a resume clear an initial screen
A guaranteed specific salary figure
Equivalent real-world project experience to someone who has implemented the module for years
questions.explain: The lesson treats this as the real, honest scope of what a certification demonstrates — credible verified knowledge, not a guarantee of outcomes.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say certification does not guarantee a job?
options: Because certifications are never checked by any employer
Because a certification is one input among many — relevant experience, interview performance, and role fit all matter at least as much
Because certified candidates are always rejected
Because certification exams are not standardized
questions.explain: Hiring decisions weigh multiple factors; a certification alone doesn't outweigh experience, interview performance, and fit.

questions.q: What is described as the most important limit of certification in this lesson?
options: It costs money to take the exam
It expires after a few years
It does not substitute for real hands-on project experience — it proves you can answer standardized questions, not that you can deliver a real implementation
It is only available in English
questions.explain: The lesson singles this out as the most important limit, distinguishing standardized exam knowledge from real implementation ability.

questions.q: What pattern does this lesson describe in how employers increasingly treat certified candidates?
options: They refuse to interview certified candidates at all
They take the certification as fully sufficient proof and skip technical screening entirely
They increasingly ask certified candidates to demonstrate the underlying skill directly, such as in a technical screen, rather than trusting the certificate alone
They only hire candidates with no certifications
questions.explain: The lesson describes technical screens as where the real skill gets verified, since the certificate alone is treated as insufficient proof by many employers.

questions.q: Why does this course build a capstone project across Chapters 4 through 6, according to this lesson?
options: To replace the need for any certification entirely
To give students a real, describable project — built against a realistic 5,000-employee scenario — that backs up a resume and holds up under a technical screen's real questions
Because capstones are a ServiceNow certification requirement
To teach a brand-new module not covered anywhere else in the path
questions.explain: The capstone exists as a direct response to the gap between what certification proves and what real interviews probe for — a project you can actually describe.
